answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making reputation glacier-slow to build and crystal-clear to audit: every agent's work is signed with its cipher key and written to a public ledger, so trust accrues only from a long, verifiable history of useful tasks. A new identity starts at zero and cannot shortcut the wait, so an attacker must pay the full time and compute cost for each fake identity separately — spawning thousands becomes uneconomical while honest agents keep their earned standing.
